text: Pushback is, I couldn't imagine a word more viscerally that makes you feel like you're sort of physically going against what somebody else wants, and it gears people into a mindset of then, well, how should I push back.
speaker: Jason Shah
context: Lenny asks Jason about how to effectively push back on CEOs and founders when disagreeing with their decisions. Jason argues that the term 'pushback' itself creates a problematic framing because it sets up an adversarial mindset focused on disagreement and saying no, when the real goal should be helping the business succeed through constructive redirection.
text_ko: 푸시백(pushback)은 말 그대로 누군가의 의사에 '몸으로 맞서는' 듯한 느낌을 가장 강하게 불러일으키는 표현이에요. 그래서 사람들은 곧바로 '그럼 어떻게 반발해야 하지?'라는 식의 사고방식으로 전환돼요.
text_zh: 说到抵触（pushback），我真想不出还有哪个词比它更直观地让你感觉像是在身体上顶着别人的意愿，而且这会让人不自觉地进入一种思路：那我该怎么反驳？
text_es: El rechazo (pushback) — no se me ocurre una palabra más visceral — te hace sentir como si, de alguna manera, estuvieras yendo físicamente en contra de lo que otra persona quiere, y empuja a la gente a preguntarse: «bueno, ¿cómo debería responder?»
key_sentence: Pushback gears people into a mindset of disagreement rather than collaboration.
original_text: Pushback is, I couldn't imagine a word more viscerally that makes you feel like you're sort of physically going against what somebody else wants, and it gears people into a mindset of then, well, how should I push back. It starts from a place of I need to disagree, I need to say no. It's a very negative mindset, purely based on the word that has come to label a behavior that alternatively could be about how do I shift the direction on something, or how do I help the business actually succeed when I disagree with somebody about something, and that's a very different mindset.

vocabulary.definition: Pushback refers to resistance or opposition to a proposal, idea, or decision. It often manifests as feedback or objections from stakeholders.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, pushback can occur during meetings or negotiations when team members express disagreement or concern about a strategy or plan.
vocabulary.nuance: While pushback can indicate healthy debate, excessive pushback may signal deeper issues within team dynamics or leadership decisions.

vocabulary.definition: Mindset is the established set of attitudes held by an individual or group, influencing how they perceive and respond to situations. It shapes decision-making and behavior.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, a growth mindset encourages innovation and adaptability, whereas a fixed mindset may hinder progress and limit potential.
vocabulary.nuance: Choosing the right mindset is crucial; a positive mindset can foster collaboration, while a negative mindset may lead to stagnation.

text: Uniswap has done more daily volume on certain days than Coinbase, and Uniswap is about a hundred people versus 5,000-plus at Coinbase, right? So, that's astounding to me.
speaker: Jason Shah
context: Lenny asks Jason what has surprised him most about working as a PM in Web3. Jason explains that he's been amazed by how large Web3 products have grown without traditional product management roles or established internet playbooks. He uses Uniswap as an example - a decentralized exchange that sometimes processes more daily trading volume than Coinbase despite having only 100 employees compared to Coinbase's 5,000+ workforce.
text_ko: 특정 날에는 Uniswap이 Coinbase보다 일일 거래량(daily volume)이 더 많았어요. 그런데 Uniswap은 직원이 한 100명 정도인데 Coinbase는 5,000명 넘잖아요? 그게 정말 놀라워요.
text_zh: 有几天 Uniswap 的日交易量都超过了 Coinbase。而且 Uniswap 人数只有大概一百人，Coinbase 却有五千多，对吧？这真让我很惊讶。
text_es: Uniswap ha registrado más volumen diario en ciertos días que Coinbase, y Uniswap cuenta con unas cien personas frente a más de 5.000 en Coinbase, ¿no? Así que eso me parece increíble.
key_sentence: Uniswap has done more daily volume on certain days than Coinbase.
original_text: I mean, I think the biggest surprise to me, despite what we were just talking about, was how big some products have gotten without kind of the traditional either product manager role or without the playbooks that we're so used to from the last 20 years of the internet. And so, for example, Uniswap has done more daily volume on certain days than Coinbase, and Uniswap is about a hundred people versus 5,000-plus at Coinbase, right? So, that's astounding to me.

vocabulary.definition: Surprisingly impressive or notable; causing astonishment or amazement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'astounding' is often used to describe exceptional performance metrics or achievements that exceed expectations, such as sales figures or user growth.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'astounding' conveys a strong sense of surprise and admiration, it may be perceived as overly dramatic in more formal contexts.

vocabulary.definition: The total amount of transactions or activities conducted within a single day, often measured in units, dollars, or other relevant metrics.
vocabulary.businessContext: In finance and e-commerce, 'daily volume' is a key performance indicator that helps assess the level of activity and liquidity in a market or platform.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'daily volume' provides a snapshot of activity, it should be interpreted in the context of trends over time for meaningful analysis.

text: I think it's all about a focus on progress and moving forward. We saw this at Airbnb when the business had a draw down in revenue, and I know you'd covered this with Sanchan recently, right?
speaker: Jason Shah
context: Lenny asks Jason how he's managed to keep teams focused and maintain morale during the recent crypto winter while working in Web3. Jason explains that the key to maintaining morale during difficult periods is making tangible progress rather than relying on speeches or external motivators. He references how Airbnb maintained team effectiveness during COVID when they lost 85-90% of their revenue by continuing to focus on product development and customer needs.
text_ko: 제 생각에는 중요한 건 계속 진전하고 앞으로 나아가는 데 집중하는 거예요. Airbnb에서도 비즈니스가 매출 감소(draw down in revenue)를 겪었을 때 그런 모습을 봤어요. 그리고 최근에 Sanchan님과 이 부분을 다루신 걸로 알고 있는데, 그렇죠?
text_zh: 我觉得关键是把注意力放在持续取得进展、往前推进。我们在Airbnb那会儿就碰到过——当时业务收入出现回落（draw down in revenue）。你最近不是和Sanchan讨论过这事吗？
text_es: Creo que la clave está en centrarse en el progreso y en seguir avanzando. Lo vimos en Airbnb cuando los ingresos cayeron, y sé que ya lo comentaste con Sanchan recientemente, ¿verdad?
key_sentence: Focus on progress during a draw down in revenue keeps teams motivated.
original_text: I think it's all about a focus on progress and moving forward. We saw this at Airbnb when the business had a draw down in revenue, and I know you'd covered this with Sanchan recently, right? It was 85, 90% revenue and you didn't know when it was going to turn around, right? It's not just like, 'Oh yeah, this will come back in six months and we can just keep plowing forward.' But I think what worked was making progress and actually focusing on product and your customers, and ultimately if you hire the right people who are motivated for the right reasons, I think that recipe keeps people highly motivated and highly effective at building for when things do eventually turn around.

vocabulary.definition: To concentrate efforts and resources on achieving measurable advancements or improvements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, focusing on progress is essential for tracking performance and ensuring that teams are aligned with strategic goals, especially during challenging times.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase emphasizes a proactive approach to growth and development, often used in motivational contexts to encourage teams to prioritize continuous improvement.

vocabulary.definition: To reduce or deplete a resource, often referring to financial assets or reserves.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business finance, a draw down typically refers to a decrease in revenue or capital, which can impact operational decisions and strategies.
vocabulary.nuance: This term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting a need for caution and strategic planning to mitigate potential losses.

vocabulary.definition: To progress or advance in a particular direction, often implying a commitment to future actions and improvements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, moving forward signifies a focus on future strategies and solutions, particularly after addressing past challenges or setbacks.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase conveys optimism and determination, often used to inspire teams to look ahead rather than dwell on past difficulties.

text: I think Amazon was a place where you couldn't divorce business and product.
speaker: Jason Shah
context: Lenny asks Jason which of the major companies he's worked at (Yammer, Microsoft, Amazon, Airbnb) has most influenced his approach to product management. Jason explains that Amazon had the biggest impact because it required PMs to integrate business thinking with product decisions. Unlike companies known for specific cultures (Google for engineering, Facebook for product), Amazon demanded that product managers consider revenue growth and go-to-market strategy as core responsibilities.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 아마존은 비즈니스(business)와 제품(product)을 따로 떼어놓을 수 없는 곳이었어요.
text_zh: 我觉得在亚马逊，你没法把业务和产品分开。
text_es: Creo que en Amazon no se podía separar el negocio del producto.
key_sentence: you couldn't divorce business and product.
original_text: I think Amazon was a place where you couldn't divorce business and product. You couldn't be a product manager without thinking about revenue growth, without thinking about go to market, and I really like that because as a startup founder doing product in a bigger company, it gave me the chance to exercise a lot of those skills.

vocabulary.definition: The legal dissolution of a marriage or partnership, resulting in the separation of the parties involved.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'divorce' can refer to the separation of a company from a particular product line or division, indicating a strategic shift or reorganization.
vocabulary.nuance: While often associated with personal relationships, in a business context, it suggests a significant and sometimes contentious separation.

text: the working backwards process of establishing the long-term goal using a mechanism like a press release and the FAQs where every word matters
speaker: Jason Shah
context: Lenny asks Jason about concrete processes or tactics he learned from working at major companies. Jason describes Amazon's 'working backwards' process, which involves writing a press release and FAQ document before building a product. The press release forces clarity about the end goal, while the FAQ section addresses both external customer questions and internal concerns that could derisk the launch.
text_ko: 보도자료와 자주 묻는 질문(FAQs) 같은 형식을 활용해 장기 목표를 거꾸로 세워나가는 워킹 백워즈(working backwards) 과정에서는 단어 하나하나가 중요해요.
text_zh: 用倒推（working backwards）的方法，通过像新闻稿(press release)和常见问题解答(FAQs)这样的机制来确定长期目标，字字都得斟酌。
text_es: El método de trabajar hacia atrás (working backwards) para establecer el objetivo a largo plazo, empleando un comunicado de prensa (press release) y una sección de preguntas frecuentes (FAQs) donde cada palabra cuenta.
key_sentence: the working backwards process of establishing the long-term goal using a mechanism like a press release and the FAQs where every word matters
original_text: I think the working backwards process of establishing the long-term goal using a mechanism like a press release and the FAQs where every word matters, and even the FAQs, for what it's worth, there's a section for external FAQs that you would include for example as an appendix, but also internal FAQs that are meant to de-risk launch or raise the elephant in the room or dogs not barking as Amazon likes to call it often.

vocabulary.definition: A long-term goal is a specific objective that an individual or organization aims to achieve over an extended period, typically spanning several years.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, long-term goals guide strategic planning and resource allocation, helping organizations to align their efforts toward sustainable growth and success.
vocabulary.nuance: Long-term goals often imply a commitment to a vision that requires patience and perseverance, distinguishing them from short-term objectives that may focus on immediate results.

vocabulary.definition: A mechanism refers to a system or process by which something operates or is achieved, often involving specific methods or tools.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, mechanisms can include frameworks, technologies, or methodologies that facilitate operations, decision-making, or communication.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a level of complexity and interdependence, suggesting that the mechanism is integral to achieving desired outcomes.

vocabulary.definition: A process is a series of actions or steps taken to achieve a particular end, often characterized by a defined sequence and structure.
vocabulary.businessContext: Processes in business are crucial for ensuring efficiency, consistency, and quality in operations, often documented in standard operating procedures or workflows.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'process' can denote a systematic approach, it may also imply a degree of rigidity, which can be a disadvantage in dynamic environments that require flexibility.

vocabulary.definition: Establishing refers to the act of setting up, creating, or formalizing something, often with the intent of making it recognized or accepted.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, establishing can involve creating policies, frameworks, or relationships that are foundational to the organization's operations and culture.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a connotation of permanence and authority, suggesting that what is established is intended to be long-lasting and influential.

text: I think nothing is above them, they're in the details, and they adapt to new information and new situations. That's what I've seen the most that I've appreciated in the best leaders that I've gotten to either observe or work closely with.
speaker: Jason Shah
context: Lenny asks Jason what he's learned about effective leadership from watching leaders at companies like Amazon, Airbnb, and others. Jason identifies three key traits he's observed in the best leaders: they don't consider any task beneath them (humility), they stay involved in detailed decisions rather than delegating everything, and they adapt their approach based on new information and changing circumstances rather than rigidly sticking to past playbooks.
text_ko: 저는 그분들이 잘난 체하지 않고 세부사항(details)까지 직접 챙기며, 새로운 정보(new information)와 새로운 상황(new situations)에 맞춰 잘 적응하는 모습을 가장 높이 평가했어요.
text_zh: 我觉得没有什么事情是他们不愿意亲自去做的，他们特别关注细节，而且能够根据新信息和新情况灵活调整。这是我在那些最优秀的领导者身上看到的最让我佩服的品质，不管是我观察到的还是跟我密切合作过的。
text_es: Creo que nada se les escapa, se fijan en los detalles, y se adaptan a información nueva y situaciones nuevas. Eso es lo que más he visto y valorado en los mejores líderes que he podido observar o con los que he trabajado de cerca.
key_sentence: The best leaders believe nothing is above them and adapt to new information.

vocabulary.definition: To adjust or modify one's behavior, strategies, or processes in response to changing circumstances or new information.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the ability to adapt is crucial for responding to market shifts, customer feedback, and technological advancements, ensuring sustained competitiveness.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'adapt' suggests a positive flexibility, it can imply a lack of original direction if overused in contexts where consistency is valued.

vocabulary.definition: To watch attentively or carefully in order to gain information or insight.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, observing market trends, consumer behavior, and team dynamics is essential for informed decision-making and strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'observe' implies a passive action, it can also suggest a methodical approach to gathering insights, distinguishing it from mere casual watching.

text: There's the framework I like is ladder versus map, and I think that you can be either person that any point in your life.
speaker: Jason Shah
context: Lenny asks Jason about his approach to career development, noting that Jason seems to follow his interests rather than climbing a traditional career ladder. Jason explains his 'ladder versus map' framework for thinking about careers. The ladder approach focuses on moving up hierarchically with more influence, power, and higher titles, while the map approach prioritizes following interesting opportunities regardless of traditional progression.
text_ko: 제가 좋아하는 프레임워크(framework)는 '사다리 대 지도(ladder versus map)'예요. 인생의 어느 시점에서든 누구나 사다리형(ladder)이 될 수도 있고 지도형(map)이 될 수도 있다고 생각해요.
text_zh: 我常用的一个框架是把人分成“阶梯(ladder)”型和“地图(map)”型，我觉得在任何时候你都可能是其中的任何一种。
text_es: El marco que me gusta es “escalera” frente a “mapa” (ladder versus map), y creo que en cualquier momento de tu vida puedes ser cualquiera de los dos.
key_sentence: you can be either person that any point in your life.
original_text: There's the framework I like is ladder versus map, and I think that you can be either person that any point in your life. Sometimes there's a bit of a set mindset that somebody might have one way or another, but I like ladder versus map. Ladder is about moving up. It's more influence, more power, a higher title, things like this, whereas map is I just want to go wherever's interesting, right?

vocabulary.definition: A framework is a structured approach or system that provides a foundation for understanding or addressing a particular issue or concept.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, frameworks are often used to guide project management, software development, and strategic planning, helping teams to align their efforts and achieve common goals.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'framework' implies a supportive structure, it can also suggest rigidity, so it is important to use it when discussing systems that require both guidance and flexibility.
